backlog.spec: After the first SLSQP solve, repeatedly perturb the best packing's centres with Gaussian noise (sd about 0.03 to 0.05), re-run SLSQP, and keep the result only if the radius sum improves. Keep the time budget and repair step.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the best packing

backlog.spec: Initialise centres on a jittered hexagonal or square-ish grid with n points spread over [0.1, 0.9]^2, using rng for jitter, and small equal radii. Use it for a fraction of restarts, with uniform random starts for the rest.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-like lattice initialisation

backlog.spec: Phase one optimises only the centres with all radii fixed to a common value found by bisection so the packing is feasible. Phase two releases the radii and runs SLSQP from that feasible point.
backlog.title: Two-phase equal-radius start

backlog.spec: Raise MAX_ITER from 200 to 1000 so SLSQP can reach a true local optimum rather than stopping early. Keep random restarts and the repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Raise SLSQP iteration cap

backlog.spec: Scale the objective by 1/n and the distance constraints so gradients are order one. This improves SLSQP line-search behaviour and reduces premature termination.
backlog.title: Objective and constraint scaling

backlog.spec: Pass analytic Jacobians for the objective and the constraint vector (pair distance derivatives with respect to centres and radii) via the jac argument. This removes finite-difference cost so more restarts fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Only include pair constraints for circle pairs whose centres are closer than the sum of radii plus a margin (for example 0.3), recomputed after each restart. This shrinks the constraint vector and speeds SLSQP.
backlog.title: Sparse constraint pairs

backlog.spec: After SLSQP, polish the best packing with scipy trust-constr using the same constraints, keeping whichever result has the larger radius sum. Adds a second local optimiser on the best candidate only.
backlog.title: Trust-constr fallback polish

backlog.spec: After repair, greedily grow each radius in random order to the largest value that keeps it feasible against walls and other circles, then repeat over circles until no radius increases. Recovers slack lost by the repair shrinkage.
backlog.title: Greedy radius growth post-step

backlog.spec: Replace the iterative max-overlap repair with a single pass that sets each radius to the minimum of wall distance and half the distance to every other circle's contact limit, processed in order. This keeps more radius than uniform pairwise scaling.
backlog.title: Replace fixed shrink with exact repair

backlog.spec: Reduce SHRINK from 1e-9 to 1e-12 and verify validity with a tolerance-aware check, since the harness allows 1e-10 slack. Recovers a tiny amount of radius per circle.
backlog.title: Remove the 1e-9 shrink margin carefully

backlog.spec: Take the best packing, pick one or two circles at random, remove them, and reinsert them at the largest hole found by sampling random points, then re-optimise. Accept if the radius sum improves.
backlog.title: Perturb-and-repair local search on radii

backlog.spec: Draw initial radii from a skewed distribution (for example a random mix of large and small values) rather than a constant 0.05, so SLSQP starts with a varied size profile that better matches optimal packings.
backlog.title: Biased initial radii

backlog.spec: Place a fixed fraction of initial centres near the square's corners and edges, with the rest uniform, to encourage boundary-hugging configurations typical of good circle packings.
backlog.title: Corner and edge seeding

backlog.spec: Allocate restarts in two tiers: many cheap restarts with a low iteration cap, then the top few re-optimised with a high cap. This spends the budget on promising basins.
backlog.title: Time-split restarts with more diversity

backlog.spec: Track the best radius sum across restarts and stop random sampling after a long stagnation window, switching to basin hopping from the incumbent for the remaining time.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart budget by stagnation

backlog.spec: Keep the top k packings. Build new starts by taking the left half of one packing and the right half of another, cut at a random vertical line, then fill missing circles uniformly and optimise.
backlog.title: Elite pool with recombination

backlog.spec: Generate some starts with a mirror symmetry about the diagonal or a vertical axis by optimising half the circles and mirroring them. Symmetric starts often lead to strong packings.
backlog.title: Symmetry-based starts

backlog.spec: Add a small positive lower bound on each radius (for example 1e-3) in the SLSQP bounds to avoid degenerate zero-radius circles and improve conditioning.
backlog.title: Radius lower bound during optimisation

backlog.spec: Move the wall constraints into the SLSQP bounds on the centre coordinates (bounds of r to 1 minus r is not separable, so use the box [0,1] on centres) and keep only pair constraints, reducing constraint count.
backlog.title: Bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: Use the current best packing as the initial point for later restarts, with small random noise on centres and radii, rather than fresh uniform samples. Keeps good structure while exploring nearby.
backlog.title: Warm-start from incumbent with noise

backlog.spec: Precompute pair index arrays and compute the constraint vector with vectorised numpy only, avoiding repeated triu index construction. Cuts per-iteration overhead so more SLSQP iterations fit in the budget.
backlog.title: Vectorised constraint evaluation

backlog.spec: Pass SLSQP ftol around 1e-12 and a larger maxiter, and check result feasibility before accepting a restart. Ensures local optima are tightly converged.
backlog.title: Stop SLSQP on tolerance

backlog.spec: Derive per-restart seeds from the master seed with a SeedSequence spawn so restarts are independent and reproducible, rather than sharing one generator state.
backlog.title: Random restart seed diversity check

backlog.spec: Within one solve call, run the restart loop in fixed-size batches and keep the best of each batch, reducing variance from unlucky initial points.
backlog.title: Repeated-run ensemble averaging of starts

backlog.spec: Add a small penalty pulling centres toward the square centre during early SLSQP iterations, then remove it for the final stage. Helps the optimiser spread circles evenly before tightening.
backlog.title: Light centre regularisation

backlog.spec: When comparing packings with nearly equal radius sums, prefer the one with larger minimum pairwise slack, which tends to give more room for later polishing.
backlog.title: Radius-sum tie breaking by spread

backlog.spec: Start with a small initial radius and gradually increase the radius penalty weight over the first SLSQP calls, a continuation scheme that avoids early jamming.
backlog.title: Annealed initial radius scale

backlog.spec: Generate many cheap random configurations, score each by a quick penalty energy minimisation, and run full SLSQP only on the lowest-energy few. This filters out poor starts cheaply.
backlog.title: Multi-start from best-of-k initial configurations

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, keep a current packing separate from the best packing. Accept a new local optimum with probability min(1, exp((sum_new - sum_cur) / T)) instead of accepting only improvements, with T starting near 0.01 and decaying geometrically to about 1e-4 over the hopping phase. Always store the best packing seen, and return that one. Keep the hop as the existing Gaussian centre jitter with HOP_SD. Use rng for the acceptance draws so the result depends only on seed.
backlog.title: Metropolis acceptance in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the objective -sum(r) with -sum(w_i * r_i), where w is drawn once per call from rng uniform on [0.8, 1.2] for each circle. The constraints stay unchanged. This tilts each local solve toward different radius allocations, so it reaches different contact graphs from the same start. Every candidate is still scored by its true unweighted sum after repair, so selection is unchanged. Pass the rng or a seed into _solve_once.
backlog.title: Random per-circle objective weights in SLSQP

backlog.spec: Rewrite the pairwise constraint in _solve_once without the square root: use (cx_i - cx_j)^2 + (cy_i - cy_j)^2 - (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0 for each pair, and keep r_i + r_j >= 0 handled by the existing bounds. The constraint is smooth at zero distance and its gradients are simpler. Keep the wall constraints as they are. Then run the existing repair step on the result, so validity is still guaranteed by the harness check.
backlog.title: Squared-distance non-overlap constraints

backlog.spec: Add a move to the basin-hopping phase. Pick the circle with the smallest radius in the best packing, remove it, and sample 500 random points. Place the circle at the sample that maximises the distance to all other centres and walls (largest empty hole, approximated by the min over distance to other centres minus their radii, and distance to walls). Then run _solve_once from that configuration, followed by repair. Keep this move with probability 0.5 and use the usual Gaussian jitter otherwise.
backlog.title: Vacancy move: relocate the smallest circle

backlog.spec: After _solve_once and before repair, identify the active contacts: pairs whose gap is below 1e-6 and walls where the centre is within 1e-6 of the wall plus its radius. Form the system of equalities for those active contacts in the unknowns (centres and radii). Solve it with a few Gauss-Newton steps (least squares via numpy.linalg.lstsq), starting from the SLSQP solution, and accept the step only if the sum of radii rises and the constraints still hold to 1e-9. This gives a much tighter local optimum than SLSQP's default tolerance, and repair then removes any remaining tiny overlap.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP call, run a short augmented-Lagrangian method on the same variables. Keep multipliers for the pair and wall constraints, and use the objective -sum(r) plus a quadratic penalty on constraint violations with weight rho starting at 10 and multiplied by 4 each outer step for about 5 steps. Each inner solve is an L-BFGS-B call on the unconstrained augmented Lagrangian. Use the output as the start for SLSQP. The penalty stage should move the start into a feasible region faster and with fewer SLSQP iterations, so the same time budget covers more starts.
backlog.title: Augmented-Lagrangian penalty continuation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the cheap _relax energy for the start generation with a stochastic compression. Begin with all radii at 0.5 times the target r0 = 0.5/sqrt(n), and for about 2000 sweeps, propose a random displacement of each centre with a step that shrinks over time. Accept a move only if no overlap appears with the current radii, where radii are then grown a little for each circle to the largest value that keeps it clear of the others and walls. This gives a jammed start that is already nearly packed and has varied radii. Pass the resulting centres into _solve_once as the start.
backlog.title: Monte Carlo compression of random starts

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, instead of jittering all centres, choose a random disc of radius 0.25 in the unit square. Freeze all circles whose centres are outside it, and re-optimise only the circles inside it using SLSQP with the frozen circles included as fixed obstacles in the constraints. Then run a full _solve_once on the complete configuration from that start with a small jitter. Accept the new packing only if its radius sum improves on the best. This focuses the search on local defects in the packing rather than on global noise.
backlog.title: Large-neighbourhood re-optimisation of a window

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform draw rng.uniform(INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW, 2 * n) in the restart pool with a scrambled Halton sequence in two dimensions, generated with bases 2 and 3 in a loop over the index. Use a random offset and a per-seed digit permutation from rng so each seed differs. Map the points into [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. Each start then covers the square more evenly than independent uniform draws. The rest of the restart pipeline is unchanged, and the pool still uses the cheap relaxation step to choose the best starts.
backlog.title: Quasi-random Halton starts

backlog.spec: Add a swap move to the basin-hopping phase. Pick two circles at random whose radii differ by more than 20 percent, exchange their centres, keep each radius attached to its index, and then run _solve_once on the swapped configuration with a small jitter. Radius-centre swaps of this kind move large circles into the slots left by small ones, which random Gaussian jitter rarely does. Keep the swap with probability 0.3 and use the normal jitter otherwise. Accept only if the best packing improves.
backlog.title: Random swap of circles of different sizes

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centre draws in the restart pool with farthest-point sampling. For each start, draw 2000 uniform candidate points in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 with rng, then greedily pick the candidate that maximises its minimum distance to the points already chosen, until n centres are picked. Then pass these centres through the existing _relax and pool-selection code unchanged. Keep the rest of the restart loop and the basin-hopping phase as they are, and use only rng for randomness.
backlog.title: Max-min (farthest-point) sampled restart starts

backlog.spec: Before the restart phase, solve the (n-1)-circle problem with a short version of the existing pipeline, using about 15% of the restart budget. Take its best packing and insert the missing circle at the largest empty spot, found by evaluating the distance-to-nearest-centre-and-wall on a 100x100 grid. Set that circle's radius to the grid value. Then run _solve_once on the n-circle start, followed by the usual clip and _repair, and add the result to the candidate pool. Use only the seed for randomness.
backlog.title: Grow from an (n-1)-circle packing

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, keep HOP_SD as a variable instead of a constant. Track the acceptance rate of the last 20 hops, where a hop is accepted if it improves the best sum. If the rate is above 0.3, multiply HOP_SD by 1.2. If it is below 0.1, multiply by 0.8. Clamp HOP_SD to [0.005, 0.1]. Keep the 40% switch point and everything else the same.
backlog.title: Adaptive basin-hopping step size

backlog.spec: Run the restart phase in rungs. Start with the 20 pooled relaxed starts and run a cheap SLSQP with MAX_ITER=40 on each. Keep the best 5 by sum of radii after repair. Then restart the best 5 from their current iterates with MAX_ITER=200 and keep the best overall. Stop each rung when the rung's time share runs out. Use the same time split as now, so the total CPU budget stays at 80% of time_limit.
backlog.title: Successive halving over restart starts

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, generate K=4 perturbed copies of the current best centres. Each copy gets its own Gaussian noise with sd HOP_SD. Run _solve_once and _repair on each copy and keep the copy with the largest sum of radii. Accept it only if it beats the incumbent. Use the same time budget, so each hop is a 4-way batch of local solves. Use only the seed for randomness.
backlog.title: Best-of-k perturbations per hop

backlog.spec: Scale the perturbation of each circle inversely to its current radius. Use noise sd = HOP_SD * (r_mean / r_i) clipped to [0.3, 3] times HOP_SD, applied independently to x and y. Small circles then move more, which lets them find new holes, while large circles stay mostly in place. Keep everything else in the basin-hopping loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted hop noise

backlog.spec: After the final SLSQP solve on the best packing, run a sequential linear programme. At each iteration, linearise all pair-distance and wall constraints at the current centres, then solve scipy.optimize.linprog to maximise sum(r) over centre moves and radii within a trust region of size 0.01 that shrinks by half when the step is rejected. Accept a step only if the exact sum of radii after repair improves. Run at most 30 iterations, then pass the result to _repair.
backlog.title: Sequential LP polish of radii

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a jamming-style continuation for each start. Set a common radius R, starting at 0.6 of the relaxed value. Minimise the overlap energy with L-BFGS-B. Then increase R by a factor of 1.01 each step while the energy stays below 1e-10, and cut the step to 1.001 when it does not. Use the final centres and per-circle radii, capped by the wall distances, as the SLSQP starting point. Keep the restart and hop phases the same.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-style growth continuation

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, pick a random subset of k = max(2, n//8) circles, chosen with rng, and place their centres uniformly at random in [0.05, 0.95]^2. Keep the other centres at their current incumbent values. Run _solve_once on the full configuration, then clip and _repair. Accept the result only if its sum beats the incumbent. Use a fresh subset each hop.
backlog.title: Subset re-randomisation hop

backlog.spec: Every 10 hops, apply a random element of the 8-element symmetry group of the unit square to the incumbent centres, meaning reflections and 90-degree rotations, and reflect the radii with them. Then add Gaussian noise with sd 0.01 and run _solve_once and _repair. Keep the result if it beats the incumbent. This keeps the basin-hopping pool diverse without changing the restart phase. Use only the seed for randomness.
backlog.title: Dihedral-symmetry restart seeding from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Replace the random-restart phase with a population search. Keep a population of 16 centre configurations (n x 2 arrays, drawn uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]) scored by _relax energy. For each generation, build a trial vector per member as a + F*(b - c) with three distinct random members and F=0.6, apply binomial crossover per circle with CR=0.9, clip to [0,1], run the cheap _relax on the trial, and keep it if its energy beats the member's. Every 10 generations, take the 3 lowest-energy members, run _solve_once, _repair them, and update best if the radius sum improves. Stop at the same time budget as before. All randomness comes from rng.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over centres with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Exploit that 32 = 8 x 4. Add a restart mode that parametrises the packing by 8 orbit representatives (centres in the lower-left quadrant, with radii shared within each orbit). Map each representative to its four rotations by 90 degrees about (0.5, 0.5), giving 32 centres and 32 radii. Optimise the 16 centre and 8 radius variables with SLSQP, using the same non-overlap and wall constraints evaluated on the full expanded packing (or on the 8 representatives plus their images). Use this mode for about a third of the restarts. Take the best symmetric result as the seed for the existing unconstrained SLSQP polish with the full 3n variables, then run the usual repair. The unconstrained polish means the final answer is not forced to be symmetric.
backlog.title: C4-symmetric reduced search for 32 circles

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve, run a staged schedule on the wall constraints. Replace the wall constraints x_i - r_i >= 0 and similar with x_i - r_i >= m, where m starts at 0.02 and is set to 0 in three stages (0.02, 0.005, 0). Each stage runs SLSQP with MAX_ITER 100 and passes its output to the next stage. The final stage is the true problem, so the repair step still validates. This gives circles room to move away from walls early, which should avoid wall-jammed local optima. Apply it to the restart solves and the basin-hopping solves alike.
backlog.title: Wall-margin continuation

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve, spread the start configuration with a few Lloyd-style iterations. Compute the Voronoi cell of each centre inside [0,1]^2 by clipping against the other centres' bisectors, approximated on a 64 x 64 grid of sample points (assign each grid point to its nearest centre with numpy argmin, then average the grid points per centre). Move each centre to the mean of its cell. Run 10 iterations, then pass the result to _solve_once. Use the same routine on the basin-hopping perturbed configuration. This is cheap, vectorised, and aims to remove clumps in the random starts.
backlog.title: Lloyd smoothing of starts before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a new basin-hopping move alongside the Gaussian one. Pick a random centre c0 and a radius rho drawn uniformly from [0.15, 0.35]. Rotate all circles whose centres lie within rho of c0 about c0 by an angle drawn from N(0, 0.3) radians. Leave the others unchanged, clip to [0,1], and call _solve_once and _repair as usual. Choose this move with probability 0.5 and the original Gaussian move otherwise. The rotation shears the packing locally, which a Gaussian hop cannot do cheaply, so it may escape jammed local arrangements.
backlog.title: Cluster rotation hop

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that cuts the packing with a random line. Draw a unit direction u at random and an offset t in [0.3, 0.7] for the projection onto u of the centres. All circles whose projection exceeds t are translated by a random vector of length 0.03 along a tangent direction of the line, which creates a shear slip along the cut. Clip to [0,1], then run _solve_once and _repair. Use this move with probability 0.3 alongside the Gaussian hop. Keep the acceptance rule unchanged: accept only if the repaired radius sum improves.
backlog.title: Half-plane shear hop

backlog.spec: Replace the single basin-hopping chain with K=4 chains at fixed temperatures T = [0, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01] in units of radius sum. Each chain holds its own current packing and its own best. Every hop step, each chain proposes a Gaussian perturbation (HOP_SD), solves, and repairs. Accept by the Metropolis rule with probability min(1, exp((new_sum - cur_sum)/T)), with T=0 meaning accept only improvements. After every 10 hop steps, attempt a swap between adjacent chains with the standard tempering acceptance. The global best is updated whenever any chain finds a better packing. This lets the cold chain exploit while the hot chains explore.
backlog.title: Parallel tempering over hop chains

backlog.spec: Start from a packing of n+1 circles instead of n. Draw centres for n+1 circles, run the usual relax-and-SLSQP pipeline for n+1 circles, and repair the result. Remove the circle with the smallest radius and keep the remaining n circles as the candidate packing. Run SLSQP once more on those n circles with the same constraints, since removing a circle frees space, then repair. Use this as one of the restart candidate types, with the others unchanged. The aim is that an overfull packing settles into a different basin than n-circle random starts do.
backlog.title: Drop-smallest from an (n+1)-circle packing

backlog.spec: Add a small reward for tight packing to the early SLSQP stage. Modify the objective to -sum(r) - lambda * sum over circles of the nearest-neighbour gap (distance to the closest other centre minus the two radii, using the current iterate as a fixed reference, recomputed at each outer iteration), with lambda = 0.01 for the first 100 SLSQP iterations and 0 afterwards. Implement this as two SLSQP calls: the first with the bonus, the second with the true objective starting from the first result. The bonus pulls circles toward contacts and may favour jammed configurations. Keep the repair step as it is.
backlog.title: Contact-count jamming bonus during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a discrete move to basin hopping. After each accepted best packing, pick two circles i and j with radii differing by more than 0.02, and swap their centres while keeping their radii attached to the original indices, so that the large radius moves to the other location. Then re-optimise with _solve_once starting from the swapped centres with the radii as initial values, and repair. Accept only if the radius sum improves. Use this move with probability 0.2 and the Gaussian hop otherwise. This tests whether reassigning the size pattern on fixed locations can escape a local optimum that continuous moves cannot reach.
backlog.title: Pair-swap of differently sized circles in the best packing

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP call in _solve_once, run a short interior-point stage. Replace the hard pair and wall constraints with a log barrier -mu * sum(log(slack)) added to the objective -sum(r), using slack = distance minus radii sum for pairs and the wall distances for boundaries. Start mu at 1e-2 and divide by 10 for 4 to 5 stages, warm-starting each stage with L-BFGS-B from the previous solution and keeping r at least 1e-6. Then pass the barrier result to the existing SLSQP call as its start point. Use only the existing time budget and the same seeds, and do not change the repair step.
backlog.title: Log-barrier continuation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the penalty relaxation in _relax with a Riesz p-energy repulsion over the centres, sum over pairs of 1/d^p, plus a soft wall term. Minimise with L-BFGS-B while p increases through the sequence 6, 12, 24, 48, using the previous centres as the start for each p. Do this for each of the POOL random starts, then keep the KEEP lowest-energy configurations and pass them to SLSQP as before. This drives the starts toward well-spread configurations with a smooth schedule, and it uses no new packages.
backlog.title: Riesz-energy continuation for starts

backlog.spec: Add a constructive start generator as an alternative to uniform random starts. Shuffle the circle indices and sort them into a random order of target radii, drawn from a uniform distribution on [0.06, 0.2]. Place them one at a time, each at the candidate point from a fixed grid of 400 points that maximises the largest radius feasible with the already placed circles, with ties broken toward the bottom-left corner. Store the resulting centres and their radii as the start for SLSQP. Use this generator for half of the restart starts, selected by the seed, and keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Bottom-left greedy fill starts

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.5 perturb the incumbent by a random affine map instead of Gaussian noise. Draw a 2x2 matrix A = I + N with N entries from Normal(0, 0.03), then set the centres to (c - 0.5) @ A.T + 0.5 + small Gaussian noise with sd 0.005. Clip the result to [0.05, 0.95] before calling _solve_once. The other half of the hops keep the current Gaussian move. This tests whether global anisotropic moves reach different basins than local jitter, while leaving the rest of the search unchanged.
backlog.title: Global affine stretch hop

backlog.spec: Add a new hop move for basin hopping. For the incumbent packing, find the circle with the smallest gap, meaning the minimum of pair distance minus radii sum or wall distance minus radius. Push that circle and its nearest neighbour apart along the line joining their centres by half the gap, plus a random factor drawn from Uniform(0.5, 1.5). Then move one random additional circle chosen from the 4 nearest neighbours of that pair by a Gaussian step with sd 0.02. Use this move with probability 0.5 and the existing Gaussian hop otherwise, then run _solve_once and _repair as before.
backlog.title: Jam-push hop

backlog.spec: Run three independent basin-hopping chains, each with its own current packing and its own rng stream spawned from the seed. Each chain runs in turn for a block of about 1/3 of the hopping time, measured with process_time. Each chain accepts a new local optimum only if its radius sum does not fall below its current value. After each round, every chain adopts the global best packing as its current state with probability 0.3 and keeps its own state otherwise. The global best is updated after every local solve. The restart phase and repair step stay as they are.
backlog.title: Island model basin hopping

backlog.spec: Add a compound move to basin hopping. Choose a random adjacent pair of circles in the incumbent. Remove the smaller of the two and enlarge the other to the average of the pair radii, so the pair becomes one larger circle. Then insert a new circle with radius 0.5 times the removed radius at the point of a 60 by 60 grid that is farthest from all centres and walls. Run _solve_once on the resulting configuration and then _repair. Use this move with probability 0.2 and the Gaussian hop otherwise. The idea is to change the number of effective circles while keeping the total count at n.
backlog.title: Dimer-split and hole-insert move

backlog.spec: Use a cheap inner hop loop before the expensive SLSQP solve. For each basin-hopping step, perturb the incumbent with Gaussian noise of sd HOP_SD, then minimise a smooth penalty energy over centres and radii with L-BFGS-B, where the energy is the overlap squared plus wall violations squared minus a small weight times the radii sum. Keep the result only if its radii sum after _repair beats the incumbent, then call SLSQP only on every fifth accepted candidate. This increases the number of cheap hops by an order of magnitude while keeping SLSQP as the final polish.
backlog.title: Lightweight inner loop with penalty L-BFGS hops

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed HOP_START of 0.4 with a measured split. In the first restart round, time one full _solve_once call and count how many fit into the budget. Set the restart phase to end when restart solves have used 40 percent of TIME_FRACTION times time_limit, but never stop before at least KEEP times 2 solves are completed. Use process_time for all checks. This removes the dependence on the time taken per SLSQP call, so the restart and hopping phases get the same share of the budget across machines and values of n.
backlog.title: Calibrated budget split

backlog.spec: Change the restart loop so that the order in which the KEEP starts from each pool are refined is random. After each pool is built and sorted, draw a random permutation of the KEEP selected starts using rng, and refine them in that order. If the time budget ends mid-pool, the solves that run are a random subset rather than always the lowest-energy starts. This adds a small amount of diversity without changing the cost per solve.
backlog.title: Random restart order shuffled by seed

backlog.spec: In the restart pool, call _relax with a per-start trial radius r0 drawn uniformly from [0.9, 1.3] times 0.5/sqrt(n) instead of the fixed r0. Starts from a too-small radius leave room to spread out, and starts from a too-large radius compress into different jammed basins. Keep the pool size and KEEP unchanged and draw all randomness from rng.
backlog.title: Target-radius energy relaxation for starts

backlog.spec: Build a start by placing n points on a random-offset, randomly-skewed periodic lattice on a torus, then map each point into [0.1, 0.9]^2 by the modulo-1 fold with a random global shift. Use this as one of the starts in the restart pool, alternating with the uniform random starts. Lattice spacing comes from the count n and rng, and no coordinates are hard-coded.
backlog.title: Torus-wrap lattice start folded into the square

backlog.spec: Keep the best 5 repaired packings seen during the restart phase. For each new restart round, draw centres from a Gaussian fitted per coordinate to the elite centres (mean and sd over the elite, sd floored at 0.05), clipped to [0.05, 0.95], with 30% of starts still uniform for diversity. Run _solve_once on the best KEEP of these starts as before. This is a distribution-based version of elite reuse, not a recombination.
backlog.title: Cross-entropy sampled starts from elite centres

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, draw each hop's Gaussian sd from a log-uniform distribution over [0.005, 0.1] using rng, instead of the fixed HOP_SD=0.04. Small hops refine the basin and large hops escape it, and the mix needs no adaptation rule. Keep the acceptance rule of keeping the best packing unchanged.
backlog.title: Log-uniform multi-scale hop sizes

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, alternate two blocks for a few rounds. (a) Fix centres and maximise sum(r) by scipy linprog over the radii, using pairwise linear constraints r_i + r_j <= d_ij and wall bounds from the current centres. (b) Fix radii and run SLSQP on the centres only, with the same wall and pair constraints. Stop when the sum improves by less than 1e-7 or after 4 rounds, then pass the result to _repair as before.
backlog.title: Block-coordinate alternation of radius LP and centre SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the box walls by a smooth reparametrisation: centre coordinates are c = r + (1 - 2r) * sigmoid(u) style mapping, so each centre lies strictly inside the square for any unconstrained u. Radii are kept as constrained variables with only the pairwise and r_i <= wall-distance constraints. Run SLSQP in the reduced variable set (u, r) and map back. This removes the 4n wall inequalities from SLSQP and keeps the rest of the pipeline the same.
backlog.title: Sigmoid reparametrisation of centres

backlog.spec: For each basin-hopping perturbation, first run _solve_once with maxiter 25 as a cheap screen. Run the full MAX_ITER solve only if the screened sum is within 0.01 of the incumbent sum. Otherwise discard the hop and draw another perturbation. This increases the number of hop candidates per unit of CPU time without changing the acceptance rule.
backlog.title: Hop screening with a short SLSQP pass

backlog.spec: Add an alternative hop to basin hopping that scales all centres about their centroid by a factor exp(N(0, 0.03)) drawn from rng, then adds a small Gaussian jitter of sd 0.01 before the SLSQP solve. The choice between this hop and the usual Gaussian hop is made with probability 0.3 for the scaled hop. Accept and repair as in the existing loop.
backlog.title: Inflate-deflate centroid scaling hop

backlog.spec: Maintain a set of rounded signatures of previously found local optima, for example the sorted rounded radii to 3 decimals together with the total sum rounded to 4 decimals. Skip the repair and acceptance step whenever a new hop lands on a signature already in the set, and redraw the hop instead. This forces the hops to explore new basins and avoids spending time re-finding the same packing.
backlog.title: Tabu list of visited optima in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Replace the isotropic Gaussian hop with a noise covariance that adapts to the basin. After every 20 hops, set the per-coordinate hop sd to the empirical sd of the centre displacements of the last accepted hops, floored at 0.005 and capped at 0.1. Keep the acceptance rule unchanged. This is a diagonal covariance adaptation, a step beyond a fixed or stagnation-driven step size.
backlog.title: Covariance-adapted hop noise

backlog.spec: Keep three start generators in the restart phase: the current uniform random pool, a Halton-style quasi-random pool, and a jittered-grid pool. Each round, pick the generator by an upper-confidence-bound score (mean of the best repaired sum per generator plus sqrt(2 ln T / n_g) times a scale of 0.01), where the reward is the best repaired sum that generator produced in the round. Run the usual relax-then-SLSQP-then-repair pipeline on the chosen generator's starts. Keep the rest of the code unchanged and use rng for all draws.
backlog.title: UCB bandit over start generators

backlog.spec: Change the SLSQP decision variables from radii r to s with r = exp(s), so the positivity constraint r >= 0 disappears and the wall and pair constraints are written in terms of exp(s). Initialise s = log(INIT_RADIUS) for all circles. Keep the objective as the negative sum of exp(s). Repair and the final validity check stay as they are. This changes only the parametrisation of the radii inside _solve_once.
backlog.title: Log-radius parametrisation

backlog.spec: After each local solve in basin hopping, find rattlers, meaning circles with no contact (gap below 1e-6 to any other circle or wall). For each rattler, sample 3000 uniform candidate points, pick the one whose distance to the nearest circle boundary is largest, and move the rattler there with radius set to that clearance. Re-run _solve_once from the modified packing and keep the result only if its repaired sum improves on the incumbent. Use rng for sampling.
backlog.title: Rattler reinsertion into the largest hole

backlog.spec: Replace the two sequential phases with alternating epochs. Each epoch lasts a fixed slice of about 10 percent of the total budget. Odd epochs run one round of the pool restart as now, and even epochs run a block of basin-hopping steps from the current best. Both phases update the same best packing. Keep the 0.8 total time fraction and the 30 s limit, and keep the time checks based on process_time.
backlog.title: Interleaved restart and hop epochs

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that is chosen with probability 0.25. Draw a random line through the square. Reflect every circle centre on one side of the line across it, then clip centres to the square. Keep the radii unchanged, then run _solve_once and _repair as usual. The move breaks the symmetry of the incumbent and lets the local solver recombine halves of different arrangements. Keep the Gaussian hop as the other move.
backlog.title: Cut-and-reflect hop

backlog.spec: For each restart start, divide the square into an n-cell grid. Use a random permutation from rng to place one centre per cell, jittered uniformly inside the cell with margin 0.1 from the cell edge. Feed these centres into the existing _relax pool in place of the uniform draws. Keep POOL and KEEP unchanged. This gives a stratified sample of centres with better coverage than purely uniform draws.
backlog.title: Stratified jittered-cell starts

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, use the SLSQP objective -sum(r**p) instead of -sum(r). Anneal p over the restart phase from 0.5 at the first solve to 1.0 at the last, using the fraction of elapsed restart time. Use p = 1 in all basin-hopping solves. Lower p favours spreading the radii more evenly before the final linear objective, which can move the optimiser out of uneven local basins. Keep all other code unchanged.
backlog.title: Power-mean objective annealing

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, add the term -lam * sum over pairs of log(gap_ij) to the SLSQP objective, where gap_ij = distance(i, j) minus r_i minus r_j, restricted to pairs with gap below 0.2 and clipped below at 1e-9. Start lam at 1e-3 and multiply it by 0.5 on each basin-hopping step, so the barrier vanishes after a few hops. The barrier pushes circles apart, which keeps them from jamming against a constraint early and can open room for a larger total radius.
backlog.title: Gap-entropy barrier annealing

backlog.spec: Build a start by splitting the square into four quadrants. Assign n/4 circles to each quadrant (8 for n=32) and solve each quadrant as a separate small packing in the unit square using _solve_once with n/4 circles. Scale each quadrant solution into its own quadrant, then concatenate all centres and radii, and run _solve_once on the whole set of n circles to glue and polish. Include these decomposition starts with the existing random starts, and keep the best repaired result.
backlog.title: Quadrant decomposition starts

backlog.spec: In the restart phase, after each round record the spread of the repaired sums across the KEEP local solves. If the spread is below 0.002, double POOL for the next round, up to 80. If the spread is above 0.02, halve POOL, down to 10. Start from POOL = 20. This lets the budget go to broader sampling when the local optima agree and to more local solves when they disagree. Keep the stopping rule and the time split unchanged.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart pool size from spread

backlog.spec: Add a start generator for the restart pool. For each start, draw a random number of rings k in {2,3,4} and split the n circles across rings with random counts (outer rings get more circles). Place each ring's centres evenly on a circle centred at (0.5,0.5) with radius spaced between 0.1 and 0.45, add a random phase offset per ring and Gaussian jitter of sd 0.01, clip to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], then pass the result through the existing _relax and _solve_once path. Use roughly one third of the pool for ring starts and the rest for uniform starts. Everything else is unchanged.
backlog.title: Concentric ring-layout starts

backlog.spec: Add a second hop type inside the basin-hopping loop, chosen with probability 0.25. Pick one random circle whose centre lies within 1.5 times its radius of a wall. Move it to a new uniform random position along that same wall (keep its perpendicular coordinate at the wall offset r_i), leave the other centres unchanged, and run _solve_once and _repair as usual. Keep the existing Gaussian hop for the other 75 percent of steps. Accept the result only if the radius sum improves, as the current code does.
backlog.title: Wall-slide basin-hopping move

backlog.spec: In the random-restart phase, draw MAX_ITER per start from {80, 200, 500} using the seeded rng, so the pool mixes cheap and deep local solves. Pass the drawn value into _solve_once as a parameter instead of using the global. Keep the basin-hopping phase at MAX_ITER=200. The aim is to spend more time on promising deep solves while still sampling many basins.
backlog.title: Per-start random SLSQP iteration budget

backlog.spec: Replace the restart phase's uniform random draw with a small CMA-ES style search over the 2n centre coordinates. Keep a Gaussian with mean m (initially the best relaxed pool member) and per-coordinate sd sigma (initially 0.15). Each generation samples 12 candidates, scores each by running _relax from the candidate and taking its energy as fitness, then updates m and sigma from the best 4 using simple rank-weighted means and a multiplicative sigma step. After a fixed number of generations, polish the best candidate with _solve_once and _repair. This is a bolder global search that uses only numpy and scipy.
backlog.title: Covariance-guided evolution over centres, then SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Keep a displacement vector v in the basin-hopping loop, initialised to zero with the same shape as the centres. At each hop, set v = 0.6 * v + Normal(0, HOP_SD) and set the trial centres to the current best centres plus v, then run _solve_once and _repair. When the new packing is accepted, keep v; when it is rejected, shrink v by half. This lets the chain drift consistently along directions that have recently helped instead of taking independent kicks, which should let it cross wider barriers between jammed states.
backlog.title: Heavy-ball momentum in basin hopping

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, on each hop choose a random half of the circles and hold their centres fixed while SLSQP optimises the other half's centres and all radii. Implement this by building the SLSQP vector over only the free centres and radii, with the frozen centres inserted as constants inside cons. Run a second, unrestricted _solve_once from that result to finish. Each restricted solve has fewer variables and should converge faster, leaving more of the time budget for hops.
backlog.title: Partial-freeze SLSQP for local refinement

backlog.spec: Per restart round, generate the pool as usual, then also apply to each relaxed start a random choice from the 8 dihedral symmetries of the square (rotations by multiples of 90 degrees and reflections about the axes), chosen with the seeded rng. This does not change the score of a start, but it changes the order in which SLSQP reaches a basin, so the pool's diversity is effectively multiplied. Use this only for the random-restart phase.
backlog.title: Random dihedral frame for each restart pool

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, run a penalty minimisation of the centres with radii fixed at the current repaired values. The energy is the sum over pairs of softplus-style smoothing of the overlap: T * log(1 + exp((2r - d)/T)), plus the same wall-violation terms, using L-BFGS-B. Anneal the temperature T from 0.05 down to 1e-4 over 5 steps, warm-starting each step from the previous centres. Feed the result to _solve_once. This removes the sharp kink of the hinge penalty and may place centres more smoothly before the hard constraint solve.
backlog.title: Log-sum-exp smoothed overlap penalty continuation

backlog.spec: Keep the top 2 distinct packings found so far. Form a child by splitting the plane with a random line through (0.5,0.5), taking the circles of parent A on one side and of parent B on the other. If the count differs from n, remove the circles with the smallest radii or add random ones at the largest gap, then run _solve_once and _repair. Apply this with probability 0.2 in place of a Gaussian hop during basin hopping. This transfers good local structure between two basins that have already been optimised.
backlog.title: Cluster crossover of two elite packings

backlog.spec: Keep the 5 best distinct packings found during basin hopping. At the end of the loop, for each of them, run one more _solve_once from its centres followed by _repair, and return the one with the largest radius sum. Also, during the final 10 percent of the time budget, restrict hops to start from a randomly chosen member of this top-5 set rather than only the single best. This is a small change that reduces the risk of ending in a basin whose local optimum was lucky.
backlog.title: Averaging the basin-hopping chain's top packings

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, replace the isotropic Gaussian kick with a kick along the soft modes of the incumbent. Build the Hessian of the penalty energy (the overlap and wall terms of _relax at the incumbent's centres and a trial radius of about 1.02x the incumbent radii) by central finite differences on the 2n centre coordinates. Take the eigenvectors with the 4 to 8 smallest nonzero eigenvalues, draw random coefficients with sd HOP_SD scaled by 1/sqrt(eigenvalue), and add the sum to the centres before _solve_once and _repair. Keep the Gaussian hop for the other half of the hops. Use only numpy linalg and the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Soft-mode eigenvector hop

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, add a quadratic proximal term to the SLSQP objective that pulls the centres toward the perturbed starting point with weight mu (for example 0.5 to 2, drawn from the seeded rng). Objective becomes -sum(r) + mu * sum((c - p)^2). Run the solve, then drop the proximal term for a short 20-iteration SLSQP polish with only the original objective. This lets the radii and the nearby centres re-settle without drifting far from the incumbent's basin. Only the hop stage changes; restarts are untouched.
backlog.title: Proximal-anchored hop SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a new start generator to the restart pool. Draw a ladder of n radii sorted in decreasing order with random multiplicative jitter. Place circles one at a time: for each, sample 400 random candidate points in [r, 1-r]^2, compute the clearance to the existing circles and walls, and put the circle at the candidate with the largest clearance (capped at its ladder radius). Pass the resulting centres to _relax and then _solve_once as usual. This gives an Apollonian-style largest-first start, unlike uniform draws or bottom-left filling. Use the seeded rng throughout.
backlog.title: Largest-first clearance insertion starts

backlog.spec: Change the search space to centres alone. For each candidate set of centres, compute the best radii with scipy.optimize.linprog (HiGHS): maximise sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs and r_i <= wall distance of circle i. Use the LP output as the score. The outer loop is a simple (1+lambda) evolution strategy with Gaussian steps on the centres and step size adapted by the success rate (1/5th rule), run for about 60% of the budget. Finish with the existing _solve_once and _repair on the best centres. This turns the radius problem into an exact inner solve and searches the centres with a derivative-free method.
backlog.title: Centres-only search with an LP radius decoder

backlog.spec: Add an annealed hop that first overcompresses the incumbent. Multiply all incumbent radii by 1.03 to 1.08 and run 30 to 60 steps of noisy gradient descent on the overlap and wall penalty energy of the centres (step size decaying, noise amplitude set by a temperature T that falls linearly from 0.02 to 0 over the hop steps). Then call _solve_once from the resulting centres and _repair as usual. Use the seeded rng for the noise. This is a physically motivated jammed-state perturbation, different from a plain Gaussian kick.
backlog.title: Langevin overcompression hop

backlog.spec: Add a line-probe move to basin hopping. Draw a random unit direction in the 2n-dimensional centre space, scale it by a step drawn log-uniformly from [0.005, 0.05] times the seeded rng, and form 3 candidate starts at t = 0.5, 1 and 1.5 along that direction from the incumbent. Run _solve_once and _repair on each and keep the best result as the hop outcome, if it beats the incumbent. Hops then use 3 solves each, so the total hop count drops; check the hop count with a fixed budget. This probes a whole line of the landscape per hop.
backlog.title: Random-direction line-probe hop

backlog.spec: Add a strip-based start generator. Choose a random number of rows between 4 and 7 and a random per-row circle count that sums to n (for example 5-6-5-6-5-5 style counts with random swaps). Place the centres in evenly spaced rows across [0.1, 0.9] in y with x positions spaced evenly within each row, then add uniform jitter of 0.03 and a random horizontal shear per row. Feed these into _relax and _solve_once as one of the start types in the restart pool, with about a third of the restart starts coming from this generator. This extends the hex-style seeding with variable row structure.
backlog.title: Randomised row-count strip starts

backlog.spec: Make the basin-hopping Gaussian kick depend on position. Compute for each centre its distance to the nearest wall, and multiply that circle's perturbation sd by a factor min(1, dist/0.2) with a floor of 0.2. Circles near the walls then move less and the interior moves more, so the kick breaks interior contacts while keeping the wall-touching frame. Keep HOP_SD as the base scale and the rest of the loop as it is. The change touches only the perturbation line.
backlog.title: Wall-damped perturbation for hops

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed HOP_SD in basin hopping with a cosine-cycled scale. Over the hop phase, the sd follows s(t) = s_min + 0.5*(s_max - s_min)*(1 + cos(2*pi*k(t)/T_cycle)), with s_max = 0.08, s_min = 0.005 and T_cycle set to about 15 hops, so the scale restarts high after each cycle. When a hop improves the incumbent, reset the cycle phase to the start of a high-scale phase. This is a warm-restart schedule over step size, distinct from the adaptive or log-uniform variants.
backlog.title: Cyclic cosine hop-scale schedule

backlog.spec: Run 4 basin-hopping chains with different hop sds (drawn from [0.01, 0.08] using the seeded rng) from 4 different restart packings. Every 10 hops, the chain with the worst best-sum copies the state (packing and hop sd) of the chain with the best best-sum, then perturbs its hop sd by a factor exp(N(0, 0.2)). The best packing over all chains is returned. Each hop is one _solve_once plus _repair as before. This population-based training moves the step size and the chain state together, combining the island and adaptive ideas in a way the earlier single-chain tests did not cover.
backlog.title: Population-based exploit-and-explore chains

backlog.spec: Before the random-restart loop, run scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on the penalty energy of the 2n centre coordinates (radius fixed at 0.5/sqrt(n), wall and pair overlap penalties as in _relax), with maxiter set so the stage uses about 25 percent of the time budget and seed=seed. Pass its best point to _solve_once as one extra start, and keep the restart and hop phases unchanged. This adds a simulated-annealing style global search that the code has never used.
backlog.title: Dual-annealing global stage before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the L-BFGS-B call in _relax with a numpy Adam loop (about 300 steps, learning rate 0.01 decaying to 0.001) on the same overlap and wall penalty energy. Analytic gradients are easy to write for the pair term and the wall term. Multiply the penalty weight by 1.02 every 30 steps so the configuration is pushed from loose to jammed. The rest of the restart pool logic stays the same.
backlog.title: Adam penalty descent as a start generator

backlog.spec: After the relaxed start is built, move the circle with the largest current radius to the corner (r, r) and exclude its two coordinates from the SLSQP variables, so the solver works on 2n-2 centre coordinates plus n radii. This removes the translation and reflection degeneracy of the square and shrinks the search space. Apply it in _solve_once for every restart and hop call, and reinsert the fixed coordinates before repair.
backlog.title: Anchor the largest circle at a corner

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, draw K=4 jittered copies of the start centres (Gaussian sd 0.01, from the seeded rng) and solve one SLSQP problem whose objective is the negative sum of radii averaged over the copies, with shared radii and each copy's pair and wall constraints. Use the averaged solution as the start for a final unjittered SLSQP solve. The aim is to escape narrow basins by smoothing the feasible region, so the restart phase gets a different kind of local optimum.
backlog.title: Randomised-smoothing SLSQP over jittered copies

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform draw of initial centres in the restart pool with samples from a Beta(0.7, 0.7) distribution per coordinate, mapped into [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. This puts more starts near the walls and corners, where dense packings of 32 circles usually have their boundary circles. Keep the pool size, the _relax step and the KEEP selection unchanged. The change is one line in the sampling expression.
backlog.title: Beta-distributed edge-biased starts

backlog.spec: Each restart round, split the square by a random vertical or horizontal line into two rectangles, and solve a packing of about n/2 circles in each with _solve_once after rescaling its coordinates to the unit square. Map both results back to the full square, concatenate them into n circles, and run one SLSQP solve on the combined configuration before repair. Keep the best result as a candidate for the basin-hopping start. This is a constructive merge, not a random start.
backlog.title: Half-square merge of two sub-packings

backlog.spec: Keep every repaired restart result in a list instead of only the best. Before basin hopping, sample the starting packing from a softmax over the repaired radius sums with temperature 0.02, using the seeded rng. Basin hopping then starts from that sample rather than always from the single maximum. This is a cheap way to spread effort over several good basins without adding a new move type.
backlog.title: Boltzmann selection among restart results

backlog.spec: Add to the SLSQP objective a term -lambda times the sum of radius times the squared distance of each centre to (0.5, 0.5), with lambda annealed from 0.05 to 0 over three SLSQP calls. Each call starts from the previous solution. The final call is the plain objective, so the result is still a maximum of the sum of radii, but the first calls favour compact configurations that leave room for more radius. This is a continuation in the objective, not a new constraint.
backlog.title: Penalty-weight homotopy in the SLSQP objective

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed Gaussian sd HOP_SD for every centre, draw each hop's perturbation as sd proportional to the local slack, computed as the distance from each centre to its nearest neighbour minus the sum of the two radii, clipped to [0.2, 2] times HOP_SD. Circles with much room move more, and jammed ones move less. Keep the rest of the basin-hopping loop and the best-update rule unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-scale rescaling of the basin-hopping step

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 40 percent split with a loop of rounds of 10 percent of the budget: each round runs one restart pool and then one basin-hopping chunk of equal length from the current best, and the loop stops at the budget. Use the round index to select the pool size, with POOL = 10 for early rounds and 20 for late ones. This does not add moves, it only interleaves the two existing phases with a fixed, simple split.
backlog.title: Lexicographic restart and polish schedule

backlog.spec: In the restart pool, replace the penalty relaxation for a third of the starts with a max-min dispersion solve: maximise a soft-min of pairwise centre distances plus boundary distances, implemented as minimising a log-sum-exp energy of -distance terms with L-BFGS-B. Increase the sharpness parameter beta in 3 steps (e.g. 5, 20, 80) with a warm start between steps. Initial radii for SLSQP are half the nearest-neighbour distance, clipped to the walls. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged and draw all randomness from the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Log-sum-exp dispersion starts

backlog.spec: Add a start generator that places the n centres on a golden-angle (Vogel) spiral, p_k = 0.5 + s * sqrt(k + 0.5) * (cos(k * 2.39996...), sin(k * 2.39996...)) scaled to fit inside [0.1, 0.9]^2, then maps the points to the square by a radial rescale. Apply a random rotation angle, a random spiral scale s in [0.6, 1.0], and a jitter of sd 0.02 drawn from the seed. Use these as a fraction (about 25%) of the restart pool starts, relaxed with the existing _relax before SLSQP. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Vogel sunflower spiral starts

backlog.spec: After each _relax call in the pool, round the minimised energy to 1e-7 and keep a set of seen values. Skip the SLSQP solve for any start whose relaxed energy matches one already solved, since identical relaxed minima will give identical SLSQP results. Refill the pool with fresh uniform draws until KEEP distinct starts are collected, so the time saved goes to new basins. Cap the total number of draws per round to avoid an endless loop.
backlog.title: Relaxed-energy dedupe in the restart pool

backlog.spec: Before the random-restart SLSQP phase, run one extra SLSQP for each start in which all radii are tied to a single shared variable t and the objective is maximise t subject to the same non-overlap and wall constraints with r_i = t. This gives a feasible equal-radius packing that is far from the sum-optimal basin. Pass its centres, with radii initialised at t, into the normal SLSQP that maximises the sum. Use the same MAX_ITER and keep the existing repair step.
backlog.title: Max-min equal-radius pre-stage

backlog.spec: Generate a share of restart starts (about one third) that are symmetric under reflection across the diagonal y = x. Draw n/2 centres uniformly in the lower triangle and mirror them to (y, x). For odd n, put the extra centre on the diagonal at a random position. The mirrored starts are relaxed with the existing _relax and then optimised by SLSQP without any symmetry constraint, so the solver is free to break symmetry. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Diagonal-mirror symmetric starts

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, replace the acceptance test r.sum() > best[1].sum() with a lexicographic comparison of the descending-sorted radius vectors, using a tolerance of 1e-9 on the sum first and then comparing the sorted vectors element by element. This prefers packings with a more even radius distribution when the sums are tied, which can open routes out of plateaus where the sum is flat. Keep the same hop move and budget.
backlog.title: Lexicographic sorted-radius acceptance in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Inside _solve_once, add a margin m to every pair constraint, d_ij - r_i - r_j - m >= 0, with m starting at 0.01 for the first SLSQP call and decreasing geometrically to 0 over successive calls in the same restart round. Each later call starts from the previous result. The final repair step still guarantees validity. This is a schedule over the constraint set rather than the objective, so the optimiser first finds a comfortably separated packing and then tightens it toward contact.
backlog.title: Pair-margin tightening schedule in SLSQP

backlog.spec: After each basin-hopping local solve, record the set of near-contact pairs (gap below 1e-4) from the incumbent. For the next hop, build the start from the perturbed incumbent and add a soft equality-like penalty that pulls each recorded contact pair toward its incumbent distance, with weight 1e3, in a short L-BFGS-B pass before SLSQP. The penalty only shapes the start, and the final SLSQP runs unchanged, so contact topology is carried over between hops.
backlog.title: Contact-graph warm start with target distances

backlog.spec: Add a start generator that draws n random sites in the square and n target radii from a Beta(2, 3) scaled to [0.05, 0.25]. Compute the power diagram with weights w_i = target_radius_i squared, approximated on a 200 by 200 grid by assigning each grid point to the site minimising |p - c_i|^2 - w_i. Set each centre to the centroid of its cell and each initial radius to the target value clipped by the distance to the nearest wall. Use this for about a quarter of restart starts before the standard SLSQP.
backlog.title: Power-diagram starts weighted by target radii

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP in a restart round, compute the Delaunay triangulation of the relaxed centres with scipy.spatial.Delaunay. For each triangle, take the circumcentre radius and assign it as a capacity to the nearest centre, then set the initial radius of each circle to the minimum of its capacity values times 0.5, floored at 0.02. Replace the constant INIT_RADIUS initial guess with these values for that start only. The rest of the pipeline is unchanged, and all randomness comes from the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Delaunay-circumcircle radius seeding

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the objective -sum(r) with -sum(r) + eps * (t . c), where t is a random unit vector drawn from rng for each restart and eps is about 0.02, linearly annealed to 0 at the end of the SLSQP solve by a second short SLSQP call on the plain objective. The tilt pushes the packing toward one wall, which breaks symmetry and lets the search reach asymmetric basins that the plain objective rarely finds. Keep the final polish on the untilted -sum(r) so the returned value is an honest local optimum. Only the restart phase uses the tilt; basin hopping is unchanged.
backlog.title: Random linear tilt in the SLSQP objective

backlog.spec: Add a start generator for the restart pool. Build a random sparse graph on n nodes by connecting each node to 3 random others (using rng). Form the graph Laplacian, take the eigenvectors for the 2nd and 3rd smallest eigenvalues, and map each node's pair of eigenvector coordinates to the square by min-max scaling into [0.1, 0.9]. Add small rng jitter of sd 0.01. Use these as centre starts for a fraction (about one third) of the pool, with the rest drawn uniformly as before. Relax and rank them with the existing _relax step so the cheap selection logic is unchanged.
backlog.title: Laplacian-eigenmap starts from a random sparse graph

backlog.spec: Add a move to the basin-hopping loop with probability 0.25. Pick a random direction among the four walls (bottom, left, top, right) and a random angle in [0, pi/2] for diagonal directions. Sort the circles by their projection on the direction toward the wall. For each in order, slide its centre along the direction until it touches the wall or one of its radius-sum neighbours (use current radii), then leave the rest unchanged. Feed the compacted centres to _solve_once and _repair as usual. This simulates gravity-driven jamming, which can shift which circles are rattlers and open new contact networks.
backlog.title: Gravity compaction hop in basin hopping

backlog.spec: After the repair step in solve, run a deterministic polish sweep over the packing for a few passes. For each circle i in random order, consider a small grid of trial centres around its current position (for example a 9 by 9 grid with half-width 0.02). For each trial, compute the largest feasible radius for circle i given the other circles' current radii and centres (min of wall distances and distance to each other circle minus that circle's radius). Keep the trial that maximises the total radius sum, updating r_i and c_i. Stop when a full pass gives no gain. This is a cheap nonsmooth local search with no solver calls, intended to clean up near-optimal packings returned by SLSQP.
backlog.title: Coordinate-sweep exact radius polish

backlog.spec: Add a start generator for the restart pool. Lay out a jittered square grid of about 6 by 6 sites spanning [0.1, 0.9] squared, then delete 4 random sites (chosen with rng) and add 4 uniform random points in the square to fill the holes, giving 32 centres in total. Add jitter of sd 0.02 to every centre. Use these as candidates in the pool with the same _relax filter as the others. Do not use the hex layout or the torus-wrap start, which are already in the backlog. The aim is starts that are near a lattice but have defects, which the SLSQP can then repair into different jammed configurations.
backlog.title: Square grid with random holes as a start

backlog.spec: Replace the _relax energy minimisation for one third of the pool with a short molecular-dynamics run. Start from uniform random centres with zero velocity. Use soft repulsion between circles of fixed trial radius r0 = 0.5 over sqrt(n), a wall repulsion term, and velocity Verlet integration with timestep 0.01 for 300 steps. Apply a Berendsen thermostat that scales velocities by a factor that decays from 1.5 to 0 over the run (a slow cooling). Return the final positions, then pass them through the usual _relax and rank step. This mimics a thermal annealing of the packing and produces starts with a different spread of contacts than pure energy minimisation.
backlog.title: Verlet molecular-dynamics quench of starts

backlog.spec: Keep three hop kernels inside the basin-hopping loop: the existing isotropic Gaussian step of sd HOP_SD, a step of sd HOP_SD/3 on the 5 circles with the smallest radii, and a step of sd 2*HOP_SD on a random half of circles. Choose a kernel each hop using UCB1 with the reward being 1 if the hop improves the best sum and 0 otherwise, initialised with one pull each. Use rng for all draws. Record the pull counts so the choice is seeded and reproducible. The goal is to let the search spend its hops on whichever move size currently yields improvements, instead of a fixed mixture.
backlog.title: Bandit over basin-hopping kernels

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping perturbation, with probability 0.5 per hop, draw a random axis (x or y) and scale the Gaussian step on that axis by 3 while scaling the other axis by 0.3. Otherwise use the normal isotropic step of sd HOP_SD. This makes the hop prefer slides along horizontal or vertical rows of circles, which is how many best-known square packings differ from each other, while still allowing isotropic moves. Use the seeded rng for all draws and keep the rest of the loop and the acceptance rule unchanged.
backlog.title: Anisotropic per-hop step along one axis

backlog.spec: Keep the basin-hopping chain as is, but count the number of consecutive hops without an improvement of the best sum. When the count reaches 25, restart the chain from a random member of an elite list of the 4 best distinct packings found so far (distinct means the sorted radii differ by more than 1e-4 in sum), resetting the counter. Maintain the elite list by inserting each new local optimum that beats the worst elite and is not a near-duplicate. Keep the returned best as the single top of the list. This is a simple restart of the chain from other good basins instead of a single chain that can get stuck.
backlog.title: Stagnation restart of the hop chain from an elite

backlog.spec: Keep the main loop unchanged, but store the best 3 distinct packings found during basin hopping (not only the single best). At the end of solve, for each of these 3, run one more SLSQP call with ftol=1e-12 and MAX_ITER=300 started from its centres and radii, then repair and keep the packing with the largest radius sum. Reserve the last 5 percent of the time budget for this polish, so the loop budget is TIME_FRACTION * time_limit minus that reserve. This targets the final few digits of the sum, where the current code stops once the hop budget ends.
backlog.title: Final tight SLSQP on the top packings

backlog.spec: In solve, first run the existing restart machinery on n//2 circles for a short slice (about 10% of the budget) to get a 16-circle packing. Build a 32-circle start by splitting each circle into two copies placed at c plus and minus a random unit vector times 0.5*r, with radius scaled by about 0.7. Clip to the square, then run _solve_once and _repair on this start. Add the best result to the candidate pool, keeping the rest of the restart and hop logic unchanged. Generalise the split count to n - n//2 when n is odd.
backlog.title: Split-merge start from a 16-circle optimum (bold)

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, add an upper bound on each radius that is annealed during the restart phase. Use a cap of 0.12 at the start of the round, then raise it geometrically to 1.0 by the final SLSQP iteration, implemented by running SLSQP in 3 stages with bounds r_i <= cap. Greedy early growth of a few large circles is what locks in poor basins, so the cap should let many circles settle before any one grows large. Keep the final stage uncapped so the repair and the returned packing are unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-cap continuation during restart SLSQP

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP call on each start, run a short L-BFGS-B on the centres that minimises the overlap energy from _relax plus a small weight (about 1e-3) on the variance of approximate Voronoi cell areas. Approximate the areas with a 40x40 grid assignment of sample points to the nearest centre, using a smoothed indicator so the gradient is defined, or use the sum of squared distances of grid points to their nearest centre as a proxy. This spreads circles so that no region is starved, which leaves fewer rattler holes after the SLSQP stage.
backlog.title: Voronoi-cell balance penalty in the pre-stage (bold)

backlog.spec: Replace the single SLSQP call in _solve_once with a sequence of 4 to 6 rounds. Each round imposes box bounds of half-width 0.05 on the centres and radii around the current iterate, runs SLSQP with maxiter 60, then re-centres the box on the new iterate. Stop early if the sum of radii changes by less than 1e-7 between rounds. The bounded steps keep the solver from jumping across the square into a distant basin on a single call, while the total budget stays equal to the current MAX_ITER cap.
backlog.title: Trust-region SLSQP with a moving box

backlog.spec: During the restart SLSQP, add a small penalty weight (about 1e-3) times the squared deficit of each circle's contact count below 3, where a contact means a pair gap below 1e-3 at the current iterate. Compute the contact counts once at each outer iteration and keep the penalty as a smooth function of the gaps in the objective so SLSQP sees a differentiable target. The aim is to favour packings where every circle is held by at least three neighbours, which reduces the number of free rattlers in the returned solution.
backlog.title: Target contact-count regularizer in the SLSQP objective

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, instead of one Gaussian perturbation per step, draw a noise vector z and run two local solves from incumbent plus HOP_SD*z and incumbent minus HOP_SD*z. Keep the better of the two results if it beats the incumbent. Each step thus probes a symmetric pair of nearby basins, giving a cheap estimate of which direction improves the sum of radii. Keep the time accounting identical to the existing loop so the budget is unchanged.
backlog.title: Antithetic hop pairs as a finite-difference direction

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, accept a new local optimum whenever its radius sum is no worse than the current chain's sum minus a threshold T. Set T at the start of the hop phase to 0.01, decrease it linearly to 0 over the remaining budget by process_time, and keep the global best separately as the returned packing. This is a deterministic cousin of Metropolis acceptance that tolerates small downhill moves early and becomes strict late. Keep the chain's current state separate from best, as in the standard basin-hopping loop.
backlog.title: Threshold accepting in basin hopping with a linear ramp to zero

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, run SLSQP twice. The first pass minimises the negative sum of log radii, which heavily rewards small circles growing and balances the radii across the packing. Clip radii to at least 1e-4 before taking logs. The second pass uses the current objective, the negative sum of radii, from the first-pass output with the same constraints. Only the output of the second pass is returned, so the public contract and the repair step are unchanged. The first pass costs the same as one SLSQP call, so cut its maxiter to half of MAX_ITER.
backlog.title: Log-radius objective stage before the sum stage (bold)

backlog.spec: Keep a small hall of fame of the 4 best distinct packings found so far, distinct meaning their sorted radius vectors differ by more than 1e-4 in the L2 norm. In each basin-hopping step, choose a parent uniformly at random from the hall of fame, perturb it with Gaussian noise of sd HOP_SD, and locally solve. Insert the child into the hall of fame if it beats the weakest member and is distinct. Return the best member at the end. This keeps several diverse basins alive instead of hopping from one incumbent only.
backlog.title: Hall-of-fame hop chains with random parent selection

backlog.spec: In each basin-hopping perturbation, draw the Gaussian step for each centre from a per-circle sd that is HOP_SD times a factor of 0.5 for circles within 0.1 of a wall and 1.5 for interior circles, then multiply each step by a random sign flip on one axis with probability 0.3. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged. The aim is to move interior circles, which hold the structure, more than the boundary circles, which are often at their optimal wall contact, so that hops explore the interior without destroying the walls.
backlog.title: Edge-length anisotropic step for hops (bold)

backlog.spec: After the restart phase, run a Metropolis walk over the incumbent's centres with no SLSQP in the inner loop. Each proposal moves one random circle by a uniform step in [-0.03, 0.03] and is scored by the exact repaired radius sum, where _repair is applied to the moved packing. Accept with the usual Metropolis rule at temperature T, which decays geometrically from 2e-3 to 2e-5 over the hop budget. Every 200 proposals, run one _solve_once from the current state and keep the global best under the existing comparison. The walk uses the seeded rng and must respect the 0.8 * time_limit cutoff.
backlog.title: Metropolis annealing in centre space

backlog.spec: Change the initial centres in the restart pool so that they are not uniform. For each start, first place 5 to 8 large anchor circles at random positions with a minimum pairwise centre distance of 0.3, then scatter the remaining centres uniformly. Relax the whole set with the existing _relax before the SLSQP call. Keep everything else in solve unchanged, so the only difference is the start distribution. Use rng for all draws.
backlog.title: Mixed-size seeding for restart starts

backlog.spec: In the restart-phase SLSQP objective, add a penalty term -lambda * sum((r_i - mean(r))^2) to the -sum(r) objective, with lambda annealed linearly from 0.05 to 0 across the restart rounds. The aim is to push the early optimisation toward evenly sized circles before the true objective takes over. Compute the gradient analytically or leave it to finite differences, whichever keeps the code shorter. The final basin-hopping phase uses the unmodified objective.
backlog.title: Annealed equal-radius spread penalty

backlog.spec: Before each _solve_once call, permute the n circles so that they are sorted by x-coordinate, then pass the permuted centres and radii to the solver. Undo the permutation on the returned arrays before repair. The pair constraints are symmetric, so the optimum is unchanged, but SLSQP's Jacobian structure and step path change. Apply the same ordering to every SLSQP call in both phases. This is a one-line change inside _solve_once plus an inverse permutation.
backlog.title: Sorted-coordinate variable ordering before SLSQP

backlog.spec: After each basin-hopping SLSQP solve, run a coordinate pattern search on the centres for up to 300 function evaluations. The objective is the exact repaired radius sum. Each sweep tries moving each circle by plus or minus a step s along x and along y, keeps any improving move, and halves s when a full sweep yields no gain, starting from s = 0.01. Stop when s < 1e-5 or the evaluation budget is spent. This targets slack that SLSQP leaves in near-jammed packings.
backlog.title: Gradient-free pattern-search polish

backlog.spec: For each restart SLSQP, first solve the packing inside a rectangle [0, a] x [0, 1] with a drawn uniformly from [0.92, 1.08] from rng, using the same constraints with the right wall moved to a. Rescale the centres' x-coordinates by 1/a so that the packing fits the unit square, then run one standard SLSQP in the unit square from that warm start. The detour changes the basin the optimiser lands in while keeping every final solve in the unit square. It is implemented by changing the wall constraint in _solve_once and adding one rescale step.
backlog.title: Stretched-rectangle detour during restarts

backlog.spec: Re-parametrise the SLSQP variables so that any circle whose centre is within 0.1 of a wall is represented by its signed offset from that wall, plus its coordinate along the wall. Interior circles keep Cartesian coordinates. Map back to (n,2) centres after the solve and clip to [0,1] before repair. The aim is to make the wall constraints nearly equalities, which SLSQP handles more reliably. Keep the pair constraints and objective the same.
backlog.title: Wall-coordinate parametrisation of boundary circles

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed restart pool size POOL = 20 and KEEP = 3 with a per-round lottery drawn from rng. Each round samples POOL from {10, 20, 40} and KEEP from {1, 3, 5} uniformly, with the constraint KEEP <= POOL. The round's best packing feeds the existing best comparison. This makes the restart effort vary across seeds, which is a different kind of diversity from the fixed split. Keep HOP_START and the basin-hopping loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Lottery over restart budget and hop seed

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, choose the perturbation centre as the largest circle in the incumbent. Add Gaussian noise with the usual HOP_SD to all circles, but with probability 0.5 move only the 6 circles nearest to the largest one, leaving the rest fixed. Run the normal _solve_once and _repair on the result and keep the existing acceptance rule. This is a local kick around the most constrained region, not a global one.
backlog.title: Largest-circle-anchored basin-hopping kick

backlog.spec: In each basin-hopping step, multiply all incumbent radii by 0.9 before solving, so that SLSQP starts from a loose state with centres fixed at the incumbent positions plus HOP_SD noise. Use the usual _solve_once path, which optimises both centres and radii. Compare results with the existing acceptance rule. This is a schedule-free variant of the radius-shrink starts already tried in other moves, and it changes only the warm-start radii, not the centres.
backlog.title: Shrink-then-regrow radius basin

incumbent.description: After the first 40% of the time budget of random restarts, repeatedly perturb the best packing's centres with Gaussian noise (sd 0.04), re-run SLSQP and repair, and keep the result only if the radius sum improves.

memo: Helped: only two structural changes. Slot 3 (pool of 20 cheap-relaxed starts, best refined) gave -2.9308/-2.9317. Slot 8 (perturbing the best packing after the first 40% of the budget) gave -2.9375/-2.9365 and is the incumbent at -2.9370, about the published value. Did not help: repair variants (-2.9246, -2.9331), two-tier restarts (-2.9204), warm starts (-2.9356), alternative seeding (hex, torus, strip, power-diagram: -2.9347 to -2.9365), alternating epochs (-2.9308). Nearly all hop moves and solver tweaks landed at -2.9375 or worse, within noise (sd ~0.0034). Slot 21 crashed. Unconfirmed single runs: slot 43 (-2.9396), slot 70 (-2.9396), slot 16 (-2.9386), slots 34 and 35 (-2.9386 each). Next: replicate 43, 70, 16, 34, 35, then combine any that hold up.
